summary: The text argues against limiting or sunsetting the E-Rate program, emphasizing its importance for schools and libraries to maintain essential services and avoid budget cuts. It also highlights the need for funding education rather than diverting resources to other activities.

claims.argument: Without E-Rate subsidies, schools and libraries would have to divert money from already tight operating budgets to pay for full-price commercial broadband
claims.evidence_quote: Without E-Rate subsidies, schools and libraries would have to divert money from already tight operating budgets to pay for full-price commercial broadband—forcing cuts to teachers, staff, or core educational programs.
